acceptance_criteria.evidence: evaluate_completion_claim() wraps hunter_merge_readiness_v2.evaluate() unchanged rather than restating its decision logic; the canonicalization script reuses build_learning_ledger/materialize_learning_ledger from PR #528 unchanged with no new registry/persistence/replay semantics; EngineeringContextAuthority's existing schema (v1) is extended to v2 by adding one field rather than replaced. acceptance_criteria.criterion: No Repository Rediscovery reaches the machine-consumed agent execution path, not only human-facing documentation.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Execution Economy: focused verification is used by default; full-repository validation runs only at the repository-defined stage or when concrete evidence requires it; unchanged exact-HEAD validation evidence is reused rather than rerun.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: This mission ran the full local pytest suite a bounded number of times (once per branch before push, as CLAUDE.md's push-boundary instruction requires), reusing ruff/black/mypy (fast, deterministic) for every incremental change instead of rerunning pytest per edit. The exact-HEAD validation-receipt-reuse mechanism itself (hunter_validation_receipt.py, hunter_pr_preflight.py --reuse-receipt) is untouched by this PR and remains covered by its own existing tests/test_validation_proof_reuse.py, including the RFD-416-001 regression for reuse being bound to the exact head.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Bounded Independent Review: the review opportunity has a visible state and does not wait on any single provider indefinitely; explicit reviewer failure, quota exhaustion, or timeout is recorded and does not paralyze the candidate.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Not implemented or modified by this PR's diff. hunter_reviewer_collector.py / hunter_review_orchestrator.py already implement bounded per-reviewer ack/review timeouts and WAITING_FOR_REVIEWER / REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS / FAILOVER_IN_PROGRESS / POOL_EXHAUSTED states (existing, tested by tests/test_hunter_reviewer_collector.py and tests/test_hunter_review_orchestrator.py, both untouched here). This PR did exercise that real mechanism operationally for its own review request (see AC-10/finding F-2), but added no new bounded-timeout machinery of its own.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No false READY while the bounded independent-review opportunity is still pending: a candidate is not reported fully ready to merge while a legitimately requested review has not yet reached a terminal state.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: hunter_merge_readiness_v2.evaluate() deliberately does not gate its success decision on review-authority state (explicit design comment in the source, and tests/test_hunter_merge_readiness_v2.py::test_a_new_commit_after_codex_review_stales_readiness_again asserts state stays 'success' even when review_authority reports failure) -- an existing, intentional architectural choice this PR does not change. Closing the specific gap of gating success on an in-flight, not-yet-terminal review would mean modifying this exact-head, security-critical, previously-regressed (RFD-416-001) code path; that is a real, separate piece of work this PR does not attempt. See finding F-1.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A machine-consumable Execution Contract constrains agent execution: acceptance criteria and mission scope are immutable to the worker: an agent may not silently omit, defer, reinterpret, or narrow a criterion, and any scope expansion must be evidence-gated (state why current scope is insufficient, the exact additional scope, and its cost, before acting on it).
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The scope-immutability and evidence-gated-expansion rules are now explicit entries in EngineeringContextAuthority.EXECUTION_DISCIPLINE_RULES, reaching the same compiled context as AC-2. Separately, and already existing before this PR: hunter_pre_ready_review.py's verify_claims/verify_review_request already reject any review whose claims omit one of the governing Issue's acceptance criteria -- proven by the existing tests/test_issue_412_prevention_gate.py::test_a_review_omitting_all_but_one_criterion_is_refused (Issue #412) and test_a_review_covering_one_self_authored_criterion_is_refused. This review request document is itself bound by, and satisfies, that exact mechanism: it covers all 14 of this Issue's criteria (verified via parse_issue_acceptance_criteria against this Issue's real body).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Prevention of Premature Agent Completion: an agent's own claim of completion, a final report, a passed local preflight, a pushed commit, or an opened pull request does not itself complete the mission.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: scripts/hunter_merge_readiness_v2.py::evaluate_completion_claim() has no `claimed_done` parameter at all -- completion cannot depend on self-report by construction, not merely by convention. Regression: tests/test_hunter_merge_readiness_v2.py::test_worker_says_done_while_required_checks_are_red_is_rejected, test_worker_says_done_while_pr_is_still_draft_is_rejected, test_worker_says_done_with_unresolved_validated_finding_is_rejected, test_completion_verdict_does_not_depend_on_a_self_reported_claim.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An independent Completion Gate evaluates completion against real, current, exact-HEAD evidence (required hosted checks green, governance/verification gates green, the bounded independent-review opportunity at a legitimate terminal state, no unresolved substantive finding), not against any agent's self-report.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: evaluate_completion_claim() re-derives its verdict from the same current-hosted-state evaluate() Merge Readiness uses (draft state, mergeability, unresolved review threads, changes requested, unresolved validated reviewer dispositions, candidate admission, required checks Quality Gates/dependency-review/CodeQL, shared-head attribution) every time it is called. The review-opportunity-terminal-state clause is the one piece not yet gated here -- see AC-5/finding F-1.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Automatic finding-to-remediation orchestration: a validated finding is durably captured and cannot be silently dropped or falsely marked resolved by the remediation lifecycle.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Not implemented by this PR. docs/REVIEWER_FINDING_DISPOSITIONS.json remains hand-curated (verified during this session: no automated ingestion CLI exists that turns raw reviewer output into a classified disposition entry). This PR's own findings (F-1 through F-4 in this document) are handled the same existing way: recorded here, with severity and resolution, for human/reviewer disposition.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Automatic finding-to-canonical-knowledge lifecycle: a resolved finding that maps to an existing canonical defect family is automatically turned into a canonicalization candidate branch and Draft PR, without requiring the owner to run the canonicalization CLI by hand, and without ever writing directly to main or auto-merging.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: scripts/hunter_canonicalization_candidate_pr.py implements exactly this: computes the canonicalization delta via the unmodified PR #528 authorities, and opens/updates one Draft PR on one fixed branch (canonicalization/defect-registry-auto) via local_git_push -- the channel docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-live-dpm-knowledge-feedback-loop-design.md identifies as requiring no new authorization, after that same design doc's own investigation found the unattended-Routine alternative blocked by a platform limitation (not retested here, per this mission's own instruction). Never checks out or pushes to main; no command in the module can merge. Regression: tests/test_hunter_canonicalization_candidate_pr.py (9 tests).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: One controlled, real end-to-end proof of the automatic finding-to-canonicalization lifecycle exists, using a safe representative finding.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: tests/test_hunter_canonicalization_candidate_pr.py exercises the real mechanism end to end -- real git worktree creation, real commit, real push to a real (local, disposable) git remote, real idempotency and cross-finding accumulation behaviour -- using the DFF-008 family's real invariant text as the representative finding, with only the GitHub API (`gh`) calls stubbed. A live demonstration against the production fafa33/Project-Hunter registry was deliberately not forced: materialize_learning_ledger can only reinforce an existing DEFECT_REGISTRY.json family whose invariant deterministically matches the finding, and this session's own real accumulation-bug finding (see finding F-3) does not genuinely match DFF-008 or any of the branch/concurrency-adjacent families checked (DFF-012, DFF-016, DFF-017, DFF-021, DFF-022, DFF-024, DFF-025, DFF-026) -- minting a new family requires human/canonical approval this automation must not self-grant. See finding F-4.

The accumulation-bug fix (finding F-3) is exactly a monotonicity/restart-stability fix: propose() now bases each run on the dedicated branch's own tip when it still carries unmerged content, and rebuilds fresh only once that tip is provably an ancestor of main, so repeated or restarted runs never regress or duplicate an already-accumulated candidate. Regression: test_propose_accumulates_a_second_finding_onto_an_unmerged_first_candidate, test_propose_rebuilds_fresh_once_dedicated_branch_is_stale, test_propose_second_run_with_identical_observations_is_idempotent_noop.
No authorization-minting surface exists in this diff.
No new evidence-forgery surface is introduced; the canonicalization script only ever writes docs/DEFECT_REGISTRY.json through the existing, unmodified, digest-bound materialize_learning_ledger.
connector_write_ingress is not touched by this diff.

This session found and fixed exactly this defect class in its own commits: 58da9c6/76dbe2e were originally authored/committed as Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> but signed with a key GitHub recognizes only under the fafa33 identity, producing verification reason=unknown_key on GitHub (confirmed via gh api .../commits/<sha> before the fix). Corrected so every commit's author and committer both independently resolve to the bound Farhad5778/fafa33 identity; re-verified true via `git verify-commit` locally and `verified: true, reason: valid` from the GitHub commits API for every commit now in both PR #529 and PR #530's range.

The amend/rebase operations used to fix DFF-010 replaced commits in place (git commit --amend --reset-author, git rebase) rather than stranding an intermediate commit; both branches' full histories were re-verified after the force-with-lease push (explicitly authorized) and every commit resolves to bound writer evidence.

propose()'s staleness check (git merge-base --is-ancestor) is exactly this invariant applied to the dedicated canonicalization branch: a receipt/tip inherited unchanged from an already-merged state is never treated as current, live accumulation state.
This review request document is itself the complete base->HEAD hostile review this family requires before candidate admission, produced and committed before requesting external review.

evaluate() (unchanged) already distinguishes a still-running check (status != completed -> pending) from an actual failure (conclusion in HARD_FAILURES -> failed). evaluate_completion_claim() collapses evaluate()'s three states (success/pending/failure) into a binary COMPLETION_ACCEPTED/COMPLETION_REJECTED for its own narrower question (should an agent report done), but preserves decision.reason verbatim in CompletionVerdict.reason so the pending-vs-failure distinction is not lost to an inspector -- it does not publish anything to the GitHub status API, so DFF-014's own publish()-level guarantee is unaffected. See non-blocking finding F-2 for the collapse itself.

hunter_canonicalization_candidate_pr.py pushes through the ordinary .githooks/pre-push safety boundary like any human contribution, then opens its Draft PR immediately after push rather than waiting for the hosted Pre-PR Preflight run to complete first -- unlike hunter_issue_agent_candidate_pr.py, which is itself only invoked by a workflow_run trigger after that hosted preflight already passed. This differs because the trust model differs: this script is run by the same identity that authored the content (no elevated-trust PR-opener certifying someone else's unverified candidate), so there is no privileged-attestation-before-proof gap of the kind this family targets. Flagged as a non-blocking design question rather than asserted definitively resolved -- see finding F-5.

scripts/hunter_canonicalization_candidate_pr.py and its test module both import and load cleanly (verified: full mypy run across 865 source files succeeds, and pytest collects and runs both new files without a loader error).

tests/test_hunter_canonicalization_candidate_pr.py's deterministic assertions run only against repository-owned/local state (a disposable local git remote in tmp_path); the only external-facing calls (`gh`) are stubbed in the test lane, never asserted against a live network response.

CompletionVerdict is a structured dataclass (accepted: bool, state: str, reason: str) consumers read directly, not prose an agent must parse; `state` is always exactly "COMPLETION_ACCEPTED" or "COMPLETION_REJECTED".

findings.evidence: AC-5 (no false READY while review is pending) is not closed by this PR: hunter_merge_readiness_v2.evaluate() deliberately does not gate success on review-authority state, so a PR that is Ready (non-Draft) with green required checks but a still-in-progress review would currently report success. Closing this narrowly would mean modifying exact-head, security-critical review-authority code that had a real prior regression (RFD-416-001); that is real, separate, carefully-scoped work this PR intentionally does not rush. Tracked under Issue #532 for follow-up.

evaluate_completion_claim() collapses evaluate()'s pending/failure distinction into a single COMPLETION_REJECTED state (DFF-014 evidence above explains why this is safe for this function's specific purpose). A future caller that needs the pending-vs-failure distinction should read CompletionVerdict.reason or call evaluate() directly rather than assume evaluate_completion_claim()'s two-state model is exhaustive.

Real defect found via this session's own adversarial self-review, before hunter_canonicalization_candidate_pr.py was ever proposed: propose() originally rebuilt the dedicated branch unconditionally from main, so a second finding processed while a first finding's PR was still open would silently overwrite the first finding's proposal. Corrected to accumulate on the dedicated branch's own tip unless it is already an ancestor of main.

AC-11's end-to-end proof runs in a controlled local test harness (a disposable local git remote), not against the production fafa33/Project-Hunter registry, because no currently-open, honestly-matching existing defect family was available to demonstrate against without fabricating or misclassifying evidence. This is disclosed explicitly rather than presented as a production demonstration.

hunter_canonicalization_candidate_pr.py opens its Draft PR immediately after push rather than waiting for hosted Pre-PR Preflight to complete first, unlike the trusted-candidate-PR-opener pattern in hunter_issue_agent_candidate_pr.py. See DFF-029 evidence for why the differing trust model makes this a design question rather than a violation; still recorded here for visibility.
